header.title: Grain Smuggling Risk Assessment — Port-By-Port Analysis
header.subtitle: Dark & Unattributed Cargo Vessels 90–200m • 15 May 2026 • Top 5 Suspects Per Port

mariupol.name: MARIUPOL
mariupol.description: Major Azov Sea grain terminal. Russian-occupied since 2022. Limited commercial activity but strategic grain loading point.

berdyansk.name: BERDYANSK
berdyansk.description: Azov Sea port under Russian control. Used for grain exports from occupied territories. Shallow draft limits vessel size.

feodosia.name: FEODOSIA
feodosia.description: Crimean port with grain terminal. Under Russian control since 2014. Key node in sanctioned grain export network.

kerch.name: KERCH
kerch.description: Strategic Kerch Strait gateway between Azov and Black Sea. All Azov-bound traffic transits here. High surveillance value.

novorossiysk.name: NOVOROSSIYSK
novorossiysk.description: Russia's largest Black Sea commercial port. Major legitimate grain exporter but also potential co-mingling point for sanctioned cargo.

feodosia.title: FEODOSIA — NO SUSPECTS IDENTIFIED
feodosia.empty_message: No unattributed or dark cargo vessels 90–200m detected within 50km on 15 May 2026.

key_findings: 3 spoofing events detected in the Black Sea region — SEA MARINE 1 (VN), ANLAN (PA), and MERU (GQ) broadcasting false positions off the Turkish coast near Trabzon/Batumi corridor.
7 dark detections across 6 unique vessels. EVGENIYA (RU, IMO 9829071) detected twice near the Kerch Strait/Azov entrance, indicating persistent dark operations in this chokepoint.
TRANSOCEAN BARENTS (MH, IMO 8768854) operating dark in the western Black Sea — aged vessel (1986-built) with Malta flag, consistent with sanctions evasion profile.
LANKARAN (AZ, IMO 9451666) — sole Caspian dark detection near Baku, Azerbaijan. Potential Caspian-to-Black Sea grain transshipment node.
10 AIS STS transfers detected via AIS data, all in the western Black Sea/Bosphorus approaches. 20 additional optical STS detections from satellite imagery (10 AIS-lit, 10 unattributed).
Zero Sentinel-1 SAR imagery available for this date — all-weather radar detection gap means dark vessels may be undercounted.
grain_risk: Kerch Strait remains highest-activity zone — 6 unattributed vessels in the 50km radius, all chokepoint traffic. No dark vessels detected at Kerch today.
Novorossiysk shows 3 unattributed + 1 AIS-light vessel. As Russia's primary grain port, unattributed traffic here warrants monitoring for potential co-mingling of sanctioned Ukrainian grain.
No dark vessels detected at any monitored port on this single day — a notable reduction from the weekly aggregate. However, the absence of SAR coverage means this may undercount actual dark activity.
Feodosia shows zero activity — unusual for a port previously linked to grain loading. May indicate loading pause or shift to other ports.
regional_overview: 1,056 unattributed bulkers (90–200m) detected across the Black Sea & Caspian — these represent the pool of vessels that could not be matched to AIS signals.
1,865 AIS-light bulkers confirmed via satellite — providing baseline for normal commercial traffic patterns.
Azov Sea corridor (Mariupol-Berdyansk-Kerch) shows low but persistent unattributed activity — consistent with controlled Russian military logistics traffic.

methodology: Port monitoring uses a 50km radius from port center. Suspects are cargo vessels 90–200m (Handysize/Handymax grain carriers) detected via satellite without AIS attribution or operating with AIS disabled. Risk scores factor vessel size, proximity to port, dark/unattributed status, and historical patterns. Data: THEIA satellite detections + AIS tracking for 15 May 2026. Geographic scope: Black Sea & Caspian Sea (36°–47.5°N, 27°–55°E).
